rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Set up 2 Turn Basics 2.1 Optional 2.2 Note 3 Round 4 Scoring Set up 2-player game: 6 cards / type veggie 3-player game: 9 cards / type veggie 4-player game: 12 cards / type veggie 5-player game: 15 cards / type veggie 6-player game: 18 cards / type veggie Turn Basics On your turn do one of the following: Draw one Point Scoring card from the 3 decks -OR- Draw 2 veggies from the grid Optional In addition to the above, at the end of each of your turns you MAY flip over a previously taken Point Scoring card to its veggie card side (veggie type produced shown in the corner) Note There are six different types of veggies available, which include: Tomato, Onion, Pepper, Lettuce, Carrot, and Cabbage Round End of turn, draw from the column's deck to replace taken veggies if applicable. End of Game is when all cards are taken. Scoring Score based on what your point cards tell you e.g. 1 point per carrot Veggie cards can be counted toward scoring multiple types of Point Cards. E.G. a carrot can be used for your 1 point per carrot card AND your 3 point per carrot/cabbage pair. So, if you had 1 carrot and 2 cabbages, you'd get 4 points. Majority scoring cards also apply for joint majority, e.g. if you and player 2 both have 5 carrots, whilst player 3 has 3 carrots, you'd still get the majority carrot points. For cards that score points for the fewest veggie, 0 veggies do count as fewest.

community_text:
[Rating: 1/10] Bad rulebook and misinformative iconography. Unfortunate that all cards must be taken for the game to end. Other workarounds would have been better since this just creates luck based scoring.

[Rating: 1/10] :star::nostar::nostar::nostar::nostar:  Awful. No next-turn planning since the card shop always refresh every turn, especially at high player count.  Long term strategy is pretty much get these veggies and avoid these veggies, and grab the appropriate scoring cards according to your array of vegies. No player interaction as well. Very dull. Super dull.

[Rating: 1/10] Credit for being exactly what it advertises!!! But it’s a really bland game, so only a sadistic creature would force others to play this.

[Rating: 1/10] Really boring set collection filler that's nothing more than an exercise of tactically spotting the best move for a given board state whenever your turn comes up, there's a plethora of much better small box card games out there with more engaging and meaningful decisions within the same play time.

[Rating: 2/10] Boring and pointless game, everything changes too much too fast, so chaos is high. I thought my kids will like it, but instead they were underwhelmed after the first game, as I was also... after the second play we all had enough.  One of the most overrated fillers that I know, there are hundreds of better fillers out there that have not enjoyed even a tenth of the praise this trash has received. Life is a #%&*@.

[Rating: 2/10] Quick and easy card game for the whole family, but not very challenging or fun at all.  Artwork is just meh.

[Rating: 2/10] Should be called pointless salad, what an absolutely boring and stupid game.  Cards come out at random and you pick, you might get what you want, you might score, you might not, who cares.  Rather watch pain dry.

[Rating: 2/10] [b]Scoring flexibility mistaken for depth.[/b] The rotating objectives create constant tactical recalculation, but nearly every turn is still a short-horizon question of which vegetables or scoring card produce the best immediate return. Clever in construction, trivial in ambition. A game that offers many ways to count points without giving much reason to care about any of them

[Rating: 2/10] It is so funny, that the game actually is what the title says: Random point salad with no meaning, mechanic or whatsoever. And still people love to play that piece of trash
